newsitem.title: ITALY: MISSING ETHIOPIAN SOCCER TEAM SEEKS ASYLUM-REPORT.
newsitem.headline: MISSING ETHIOPIAN SOCCER TEAM SEEKS ASYLUM-REPORT.

text.p: Sixteen member of Ethiopia's national soccer team who went missing in Rome are seeking political asylum in Italy, the Ansa news agency said on Wednesday.
The agency quoted Rome lawyer Mario Lana as saying one member, saying he represented the group, consulted him last night over an asylum request.
Lana could not be immediately reached to confirm the report.
Italian police said they were looking for 16 members, who went missing before they were due to fly to Casablanca for an African National Cup match.
"They do not have residence permits and under Italian law they are here illegally. At the moment we do not know where they are," said a police official who declined to be identified.
The players arrived in Italy on Monday afternoon from Addis Ababa and were scheduled to fly to Casablanca on Tuesday.
Early on Tuesday morning 16 members, including the coach, left their hotel with their passports and their luggage, according the hotel manager.
Seven members of the original group were still in Rome. "We have questioned the seven people remaining here but they knew nothing about the others," the police official said.
